name: Tethakon
subcategory: paralytic agent — CNS sedative-paralytic, extended duration
manufacturer: Novafold Pharmaceuticals (research compound; stolen formula in wide Shelf circulation)
description: Tethakon is a central nervous system depressant that produces deep, graded paralysis beginning with voluntary motor function and descending through autonomic regulation over approximately 20 minutes, inducing a state of profound unresponsiveness that mimics coma while preserving core vital function at minimal levels. Unlike Myovex, Tethakon renders subjects unconscious — there is no awareness during effect — making it the preferred tool for long-duration transport and storage of unwilling subjects. The compound was originally developed by Novafold as a surgical adjunct for procedures requiring extended immobility in BCI-active patients; the formula leaked to Shelf lab networks within three years of development.
effects: Progressive motor paralysis followed by loss of consciousness within 15-20 minutes
Coma-like unresponsive state with preserved cardiac and respiratory function at minimum viable levels
BCI enters low-power standby — distress signaling is suppressed but not eliminated
Dose-scalable from 4 hours to 36 hours unconsciousness
side_effects: Narrow therapeutic window — overdose causes respiratory depression and death
Subjects with BCI pain management implants may have compound interaction causing cardiac irregularity
Prolonged immobility creates risk of deep vein thrombosis and pressure injury in extended doses
Recovery from long doses (18+ hours) includes a 4-6 hour period of extreme disorientation and motor incoordination
duration: 4-36 hours depending on dose; recovery is gradual over 1-4 hours
cultural_context: Tethakon occupies a specific and grim niche in GLMZ's trafficking and coercive transport economy. Where Myovex is used for short-duration control and interrogation, Tethakon is used for moving people — across the city, across tier boundaries, out of GLMZ entirely. The Shelf's missing-persons statistics have been correlated by underground researchers with Tethakon availability in specific districts. Corpo security uses it in off-books detention operations under the euphemism 'sedated transport protocol.' The irony of Novafold's clean, clinical branding appearing on a compound so thoroughly embedded in human trafficking is not lost on GLMZ's underground press.
story_hooks: A Shelf community organizer has been mapping Tethakon distribution points and correlating them with disappearances — the pattern points to a transport hub that is definitely not on any official map, and she has 48 hours before her data gets noticed.

A runner wakes up in a Tier 2 medical facility with no memory of the last 22 hours, a Tethakon metabolite taper in their bloodwork, and a message on their BCI from an unknown sender: 'They couldn't keep you. Run.'

A Novafold internal security officer discovers the formula leak was not an accident — it was a deliberate release by someone inside the company, and the trafficking network that uses Tethakon has been paying that person quarterly for three years.
